description: Add frontend vitest coverage for the new exemption policy, and reconcile the backend so the two confirmed-benign hosts are consistent with the new policy where it applies. The backend already treats a >=200-char github issue URL as redacted (test_diagnostics.py::TestTerminalIssueUrlSurvivesRedaction pins this deliberately, and the backend already has its own `terminal_issue_url` shortening workaround for the CLI-printed link). This feature does NOT change backend redaction behavior for github.com (that would be a broader server-side XPIA policy decision beyond this frontend-focused fix, and the backend's exempt_hosts is companion-owned by design). Instead it (a) adds thorough frontend tests, and (b) updates the security spec doc to describe the new frontend host-exemption tier and explicitly note the intentional frontend/backend divergence so a future reader does not 'fix' it. If the backend test_diagnostics.py comments reference the frontend behavior, leave the backend behavior as-is and ensure comments remain accurate.
steps: Create website/src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts following the structure of website/src/test/sanitizeCredentials.test.ts (import { sanitizeExfiltrationUrls } or { sanitizeLlmOutput } from '../utils/sanitize'; use vitest describe/it/expect). Cover: (1) a real prefilled github.com issue URL with title+body+labels and a >=200-char benign query renders UNCHANGED; (2) a monitorportal.amazon.com URL with a long query renders unchanged; (3) an arbitrary host with a >=200-char query is STILL redacted (contains the placeholder / does not contain the original URL); (4) an arbitrary host with a 40+ char base64 blob in the query is STILL redacted; (5) a github.com URL carrying an AKIA... key, an ssh-rsa marker, or 20+ consecutive %XX octets is STILL redacted despite the host exemption; (6) a suffix look-alike host 'github.com.evil.example' with a long query IS STILL redacted (exact-match only); (7) case-insensitive host match: 'GitHub.com' is exempt.

Assert on the i18n placeholder correctly: the test env resolves i18nT to a string; assert redaction by checking the output no longer contains the original URL and/or contains the resolved placeholder for the domain. Follow how existing frontend tests assert on sanitized output.

Update docs/system-specs/modules/security.md in the 'URL exfiltration detection' section (around line 390): add a short subsection documenting the FRONTEND mirror's host-exemption tier — that website/src/utils/sanitize.ts::sanitizeExfiltrationUrls now splits checks into an unconditional tier (heavy percent-encoding + hard credential markers, every host) and a heuristic tier (base64-blob + aggregate length) skipped for a code-owned exact-host allowlist {github.com, monitorportal.amazon.com} matched case-insensitively and exactly; cite issue #7820; and state explicitly that this frontend allowlist is a DELIBERATE, documented divergence from the backend (whose heuristic exemption is companion-owned tenant trust, not a fixed host list) and is NOT covered by the JWT parity guard in test_redaction_mirror_parity.py.

Re-read test/test_diagnostics.py::TestTerminalIssueUrlSurvivesRedaction and its class docstring. Confirm the backend behavior it pins is unchanged by this task (the backend still redacts the >=200-char github issue URL in scan/redact_exfiltration_urls; the fix here is frontend-only). Do NOT weaken those backend tests. If any backend comment now reads as inaccurate given the frontend change, adjust only the comment text for accuracy, not the assertions.
Run the full targeted suites and confirm green.
acceptance_criteria: website/src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts exists and all its cases pass under vitest.
The new tests would FAIL against the pre-FEAT-002 sanitize.ts (they exercise the exemption + the preserved unconditional tier), i.e. they are meaningful and tied to the new code path.
docs/system-specs/modules/security.md documents the frontend host-exemption tier and the intentional frontend/backend divergence, citing #7820.
test/test_diagnostics.py still passes unchanged (backend behavior preserved).
verification: cd website && npx vitest run src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts src/test/sanitizeCredentials.test.ts
findings: FEAT-002 had already created website/src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts (10 tests) and added the Frontend-mirror bullet to docs/system-specs/modules/security.md (cites #7820, documents the unconditional vs heuristic tier split, the code-owned exact-host allowlist {github.com, monitorportal.amazon.com}, exact+case-insensitive matching, the deliberate frontend/backend divergence not covered by test_redaction_mirror_parity.py, and the no-lookbehind Safari-14 constraint). Only step 1 case (7) was missing: added a case-insensitive host-match test 'matches the exempt host case-insensitively' using https://GitHub.com/... with the >=200-char LONG_BENIGN_QUERY, asserting the text renders unchanged. Meaningfulness verified against git show 018441f32 (pre-FEAT-002 diff): the old logic was `query.length >= EXFIL_QUERY_MIN_LEN || EXFIL_PATTERNS.test(query)` with base64-blob folded into EXFIL_PATTERNS and NO host exemption, so the exempt-host cases (1,2,7) would all have redacted under the old code (length>=200) and now render unchanged -> they exercise the new exemption code path. Step 4: re-read test/test_diagnostics.py::TestTerminalIssueUrlSurvivesRedaction and its class docstring; the backend still redacts the >=200-char prefilled github issue URL (test_prefilled_variant_is_the_one_that_gets_eaten asserts scan_exfiltration_urls(rich) != []) and the terminal-variant tests still pass. Docstring/comments remain accurate (they describe backend redaction and the dashboard rendering github_issue_url from an unscanned JSON response; no comment references the new frontend exemption inaccurately), so NO backend comment or assertion changes were needed. Verification: frontend `npx vitest run src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts src/test/sanitizeCredentials.test.ts` -> 19 passed (11 exfil + 8 cred); backend `pytest test/test_diagnostics.py test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py -q` -> 52 passed; `npm run build` succeeds (guards Safari-14 no-lookbehind entry-chunk constraint). Committed as 613603b05 (test-only change; the dist/ build output is not git-tracked). REVIEW POLISH (2026-09-02 review, APPROVED/non-blocking): applied the two cheap improvements from .agents/tasks/task-narrow-exfil-url-redaction/2026-09-02-074840-review.md without changing redaction logic. (1) docs/system-specs/modules/security.md 'Frontend mirror' bullet now carries an explicit 'Accepted residual risk' note: the skipped base64/length heuristics let a sub-200-char base64 blob at github.com/monitorportal.amazon.com render unredacted (unconditional tier catches only LITERAL AKIA/SSH/PEM/Slack markers, no percent-decode), a deliberate display-only tradeoff mirroring the backend host-exemption tier; plus a note that the exempt match is port-agnostic (github.com:443 exempt), intentionally matching the backend `_dom in exempt_hosts` tier which does not gate on port, unlike the OAuth/Slack carve-outs. (2) website/src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts gained a test pinning that accepted residual as intentional: a github.com URL with a 48-char base64 'A' blob (query < 200 chars, no cred markers, <20 %XX) renders UNCHANGED (toBe(text)), commented so a future re-tightening fails loudly. Verification: `npx vitest run src/test/sanitizeExfiltrationUrls.test.ts` -> 12 passed (was 11); `pytest test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py -q` -> 6 passed (parity unaffected). Completed status unchanged.
